summary: OAuth App credentials in about 5 minutes with no review step documented; organizations may still need to approve access to their data.

approval_wait.notes: The registration docs describe no review. Organizations with third-party app restrictions require an owner to approve the app (unverified: wait depends on the owner).

prerequisites.notes: Register under a personal account or an organization you own.
Full URL to your app's website.
Up to 10 per app. Whether http://localhost is accepted is not stated on the registration page.
Only for orgs that restrict third-party app access and only to read their private data.

steps.title: Open the OAuth App registration form
steps.detail: Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps > New OAuth App (or the organization's equivalent under its settings).

steps.title: Enter app details
steps.detail: Provide application name, homepage URL and authorization callback URL. Only use information you consider public. Optionally enable Device Flow. Click Register application.

steps.title: Generate and store the client secret
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID, generate a client secret and keep both in environment variables, never in client-side code.

steps.title: Decide on expiring user tokens
steps.detail: 'Expire user access tokens' is enabled by default. Leave it on and implement refresh tokens unless your app cannot yet handle short-lived tokens.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect users to GitHub's authorize URL, exchange the returned code for a token server-side, and request the minimum scopes.

steps.title: Get organization approval if required
steps.detail: If a user's organization restricts third-party apps, an owner must approve your app before it can access org data.

scopes.notes: Needed when the primary email is private.
Prefer over repo when private access is unnecessary.

scopes.purpose: Full access to public and private repositories.
scopes.notes: Very broad; org owners are more likely to deny it. A GitHub App offers finer permissions.

blockers.issue: Organization has third-party application restrictions enabled.
blockers.how_to_resolve: Ask an organization owner to approve the app in the organization's OAuth app policy.

blockers.issue: You need fine-grained or per-repository permissions.
blockers.how_to_resolve: Use a GitHub App instead of an OAuth App.

agent_can_do: Suggest app name, homepage and callback URLs
Recommend minimum scopes for the use case
Write the authorization code flow and token refresh code
Draft the request to an org owner for approval
developer_must_do: Register the OAuth App while signed in to GitHub
Generate and securely store the client secret
Get organization owner approval where required

claims_evidence.claim: Registration requires application name, homepage URL and authorization callback URL; description is optional, and the page describes no review or approval step.
A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps, each with up to 10 callback URLs.
'Expire user access tokens' is enabled by default for new OAuth Apps.
Organizations can restrict third-party OAuth app access and owners approve apps individually.
No scope triggers a GitHub review; scope breadth only affects whether org owners approve.
http://localhost callback URLs work for development.
